verdict.rationale: Self-hosting is a fair question for an authentication and user-management product, but nothing in the evidence shows Clerk can be run on your own infrastructure. 'Deploy to your own domain' refers to a custom domain on Clerk's hosted service. The open-source migration tool and JS SDK repo are client-side pieces, not a self-hostable core. Community comments contrast Clerk with alternatives that keep auth data in your own database, which reinforces the absence of evidence but is not a documented limitation from Clerk itself.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product
